https://t.me/csetranscripts/897
         Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Dec 8, 2025 at 4:02 PM]
         Name - Ms Angel
         Interview on -08/12/2025
         Board - sheel Vardhan sir
         Graduation - philosophy hons
         Optional - sociology
         State - mp
         Other keywords in daf - sustainable crafting , mental health , netball , journaling , sexual
         harassment

         Chairman -
         come , please sit , be relaxed okay , have you taken breakfast , breakfast is most important meal ,
         isn’t it ?

         I smiled and said : right sir

         Chairman ques -
         1- Beti bachao beti pdhao should be converted to beta padhao too …
         2- extreme poverty status in India
         3- Kerala : what model it followed to remove extreme poverty completely as it claimed recently ?

         2- philosophy in administration

         Member -2
         1- philosophy of development
         2- intragenerational equity
         3- Vedanta and Buddhism di erence

             4- western and eastern philosophy di erence

             Member -3
             1- mental health issues - reasons in women
             2- Malinowski theory of family
             3- what should be done to avoid mental health issues
             4- tribal population percentage in mp
             5- sexual harassment issue in India

             Member -4
             1- Viksit Bharat objectives in budget
             2- di between scal de cit and revenue de cit
             3- industrial development issues in mp
             4- investment initiatives in mp
             5- what is your new year resolution

             Member -5
             1- what is sustainable crafting ?
             2- what kind of waste material you use
             3- most appealing product you made
             4- three fronts where mp has done well recently
             5- Indore : cleanest city reasons ?

             In the end , chairman said : Thankyou , your interview is over , it was a good interaction with you .

             For rst time interview candidates who didn’t get enough time to prepare : this was my second
             interview so i have experienced it twice 🙃 i just want to share that please don’t panic if you
             haven’t done things well till now due to paucity of time , the boards are really cordial . Revise your
             daf well , and that too on basic things like issues in your home state , strengths , developments
             etc , prepare hobby , leadership well etc . Maintain composure and patience .

             Mocks : 2

             1 at Quantel.in and other at Sankalp ias . Choose last mock the one which gives you con dence
             because that matters a lot . All the best 😇

interviews.name: nowayrunway
interviews.transcript:
https://t.me/csetranscripts/898
             Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Dec 8, 2025 at 5:33 PM]
             Name: nowayrunway

             Date: 08/12/2025

             Key DAF Details: Jharkhand, PSIR, Slums survey, Hindi poetry, JNU

             Board: Ms. Anuradha Prasad

             Questions asked:

             Chairperson:

             1. Why did you changed school from JNV, Garhwa to CHBS, Varanasi? Lack of quality
             educational institutions in Jharkhand?
             2. Findings of socio-economic survey you did in Varanasi slum area? Follow up by objectives,
             data, challenges? How did you resolved the issues?
             3. Suppose you are appointed as an administrator in that area, what steps would you take for
             their betterment? Follow up again. (Pros and Cons)

             M2: (Lady member)

   1. Views on Dowry? Why is it still practiced? As an administrator suggest practical solutions.
   Follow up questions
   2. As an administrator would you rather be "Giver of favours" or "enabler of public policy?
   3. What about making administration accessible to people? Steps, measures, initiatives.
   4. Any statutory provisions currently going on in this regard.

   M2:

   1.Private sector role in Slum rehabilitation and redevelopment?
   2. Multipolarity and it's di erent manifestations. (Why not call it unipolar or bipolar)
   3. Can we call the 21st century world - Multipolar?
   4. India's strategy and role in the same. Your recommendations as an IR student.

   M3:
   1.Recite any poem you have written. (Hobby)
   2. Purpose of poetry?
   3. Chhayawad and role of poems in Freedom movement?
   4. Give examples of poems as in di erent purpose it serves.

   M4:
   1. IMR and MMR
   2. Reasons for states lagging behind and regional variations
   3. Why is Kerala excelling and Jharkhand lagging behind?
   4. What purpose would a national law serve in this domain?
   5. Why China is ahead of India in the eld of emerging and critical tech?
   6. Comparative analysis of progress in eld of AI (India vs China)
   7. What's India doing in this regard?

   Back to Chairperson, she said "Thank you, have a good day".

   Mocks: 2- Panel ( PW- scary old men, good for pressure handling and feedback) & Vision- smooth
   conduct), 2- 1:1, Understand UPSC (feel good and con dence booster) & Paras Chitkara (Thinq
   IAS) PSIR people can go for 1:1 with him.

   P.S. - 1st phase people, they're not getting into much trickier questions right away, are cordial
   (although chairperson ma'am did a poker face the whole time, smiled in the beginning and last).
   Rest of the members were smiling and nodding while lady member was proactively attentive.

   Cover your DAF throughly, specially hobbies and leadership part (may get into follow up questions
   on this) and current a airs of atleast this month on priority basis.

   Rest assured, everything will take care of itself, All the best to everyone. You've got this.

https://t.me/csetranscripts/956
   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Dec 13, 2025 at 10:48 AM]
   Date: 9/12/2025
   Name: cadence
   Key DAF details : IFS rst preference, DU, Head of Indian delegation at an international
   conference, world cuisine, PSIR (rest not asked)

   Board: Mr. Sanjay Verma

   Chairman
   1. Welcome (my name) - he ended up mispronouncing it, so I corrected him
   2. That’s a very unique name, have you met anyone else with the same name - I thanked him and
   said that I was yet to meet another (name)
   3. Lovely. It’s so unique, I think you should patent it (laughingly, I chuckled too). 4. Who gave you
   this name? -
   4. Okay, so coming to your DAF. PSIR is your subject, can you tell me 2 concepts, one from
   political science and one from IR that have come into question in recent times? - I said that in
   International Relations, I think Liberal Institutionalism could be a good contender, because
   multilateral institutions like the WTO and UN seem to be on the back foot, and we see a shift
   towards protectionism and minilateralism. As for Political Science, sir, I think Communism as a
   concept has always been under question, especially considering the paradox modern communist
   countries exhibit - they practice authoritarianism under the garb of communism, and end up
   liberalising their economies
   5. Okay good. Have you heard of Populism? Do you think it has always been in practice or is it a
   new phenomenon? Can you give an example from the past and the present? - Sir, I think
   populism in varying degrees has been in practice ever since democracy, and especially
   representative democracy have existed. It becomes imperative to cater to the demands of the
   people, and eventually numbers end up mattering a lot for accruing power. As for examples, the
   opening up of the EIC for public investment by the British was a populist measure. And today sir
   the rise of vote bank politics could be a case in point (I purposefully didn’t cite speci c examples
   here. Figured if they wanted to go in that direction they would prod me on their own)
   6. Okay. Out of all the leadership positions you’ve listed (I had listed 4), which was the latest - I
   mentioned the head of delegation
   7. What did you buy in that country? I mentioned a wallet I had bought my mother, and told him
   that I had spent most of my money on trying di erent foods
   8. Coming to food. You’ve mentioned world cuisine. It is such a wide and open ended hobby. Can
   you answer anything and everything about the cuisine around the world? - I told him that I was
   interested in the cuisine styles of many regions around the world (listed some) and I didn’t want to
   limit my hobby for fear of what might be asked. But of course I don’t know it all. I said I would try
   my best to answer his questions
   9. Okay then, let me ask you something, if we were to combine all of North America and South
   America India would still have more diversity in cuisine - I concurred with his view, gave
   supporting examples and arguments (gave the example of delhi, old delhi has mughlai, Lajpat
   Nagar has Afghani immigrants, humayunpur for north eastern food etc)

   Member 2

   1. Do you know what animal testing is? - I said yes and explained
   2. Do you think it should be done? Are there alternatives? - I said no, and that I nd it to be
   exploitative of voiceless animals. Talked about anthropocentricity, and how we are seeing a shift
   to biocentricity now. Said there are companies which are going vegan.
   3. Asked again, what the alternatives are - I said I can only think of arti cial tissue culture being
   used to create arti cial skin and organs to test cosmetics/medicine on, but that I didn’t know what
   is actually being used. Said I’ll read up on it

       4. The di erence between growth and development. Where have you seen growth vs
       development in your own life?
       (There were a few more questions but I can’t remember them)

       Member 3

       1. What would happen to India if we take PoK back. Give pros and cons
       2. Why do you think we only talk about women’s rights and not men’s rights? - good discussion
       on this
       3. Imagine you’re at a global stage and you have to convince the other countries that India treats
       its women well.

   1. What will be the rst thing you'll do after the interview (Parents are waiting, they will ask me
   how this went, I'll tell them)

   2. They insisted on coming or you did? (They)

   3. So you didn't want them to come? (Haha, No Sir nothing's like that)

   4. There is so much pollution outside, are they wearing masks? (No Sir)

   5. Maybe we Delhites have accepted this pollution (Unfortunately Yes Sir, but things are
   improving)

   6. Okay so you're into street foods. Samosa is a famous street food in Delhi. Tell me how many
   Samosas are consumed in Delhi in a day?

   7. Don't you think Tabla is backward looking? Like it is taking us backward, stopping growth...

   M1 (Lady)
   1. Who measures SDGs in India?

   2. Tell me about 2 SDGs where we're performing good.

   3. What is CPI? Who measures it? How much is it currently?

   M2.
   1. India has contributed so much to music, instrument-wise. Can you recall about any other
   country and their contributions?

   2. Pick up any country from Africa and tell me whatever you know about it. (Picked South Africa,
   didn't know much though)

   3. How can your knowledge/skills of music can help you in services?

   4. Speak on any topic of your choice for 2 mins. (Chose Poverty)

   M3. (Lady)
   1. Following from what I spoke about poverty - What will you do if you're in services for schooling
   poor kids? (I talked about them in the previous question)

   2. How can we make education more interesting?

   3. You must have listened about Judicial Overreach. Have you also listened or seen Lawyers
   Overreach? Can Dabang Lawyers in uence Judiciary?

   4. You've written about observing human behaviour. Have you observed anything about anyone
   here? (Told them my observation. President Sir said it looks like a pickup line. We all laughed)

   M4.
   1. What is inactive communication? Examples?

   2. Then what is the communication between a baby and mother? (Said something beyond
   science. Couldn't get the right word, so said like some magic)

   Don't remember any more questions

   President.
   So you mentioned about Magic. Magic is something beyond science. So how will you explain the
   communication between the baby and mother?

   Thank you.....

   Smiled and greeted everyone. ☺

   My Observation: Board was very cordial. One moment where I took pause or got stuck maybe,
   M4 said that You're doing good. Stay calm and continue. I was told by M2 at least 3-4 times that
   you can take pause, think and then answer. Most Members had a smile on their faces. It felt like a
   privileged conversation with very respected and senior people. For me, it was literally a test of
   PERSONALITY!

   Mocks: PW, ALS IAS, Sankalp, Vajirao and Reddy (in order). I found mocks as a necessary step to
   perform well in the interview. Not all of them were good, but I learned something from every mock.

        Chairperson
        1. You read children’s classics? Is there a child inside you? (asked with a smile)
        Answer: I smiled and said yes, sir.
        2. Which Indian English authors do you like, except Ruskin Bond?
        Answer: Sir, I primarily read Western authors, and among Indian authors I have only read Ruskin

        Answer: I said my father.
        They all laughed and smiled.
        They said they understand, but asked me to name someone else.
        I thought carefully and said Shripal Sabnis, former Chairperson of the Marathi Sahitya Sammelan.

        Member 1
        1. Why did you spend so much time preparing for the civil services? How have you contributed to
        this country in these youthful years?

        The money trail is received from the CFCFRMS module of NCRP under MHA and from there if the
        state police/ complaint forwards the list of involved bank accounts with the RBI, we make sure the
        mentioned bank accounts are checked for KYC/AML compliance and the required actions are
        taken as per the directions. Also, we are working on a draft SOP for banks in consultation with the
        MHA with respect to the cyber fraud cases after the recent Kerala High Court judgement and
        earlier Nagpur High Court bench regarding freezing of bank accounts by the banks.

        M2: So you mentioned that KYC is done in the banks. Why is it necessary?

        *Sir, there are multiple reasons for this. One is to ensure the lawful use of banking services by the
        lawful people.
        Another one is that it helps in e ectively supervising the bank accounts like Suspicious
        Transactions are reported if anything unusual happens or of they are being used mule accounts.
        For example, if in the current account opening if I’m showing my yearly income of about 5 lakh
        and suddenly I get 1 crore in my account. That generates an alert whether the account is being
        used for illegal activities or is it a genuine transaction. So customer pro ling through KYC
        becomes a useful tool for safe banking.

        M2: Okay so you mentioned about mule accounts. Why are they used?

        *Sir, mule accounts acts as the rented bank accounts which are used for illegal transactions
        involving a fraud or a money laundering.

        M2: Okay, so recently RBI is reducing its repo rate, why is it doing so and is it getting passed on
        to the customers?

        *Sir, Repo rate acts as one of the quantitative tool in hand of the RBI for liquidity management. In
        the rst half of FY2025-26, India recorded a growth rate of 8.0% and the in ation of about 3.3%
        was well within the targeted range that the MPC has set that is 4+_2%. So it was a prudent step
        to push for increasing liquidity in the market while supporting the growth perspective in this
        unique goldilocks period in India. Sadly, it’s not passed on to the customers immediately and
        proportionally . So it’s a challenge in transmission of policy rates to the customers.

        M2: Why there is so less interest rate on the deposits?

        *Sir, the there is no interest paid on the deposits in the current account but when it comes to the
        savings deposits, it is less because the savings deposits acts one of the source of liquidity for the
        banks and this spread which is the di erence between interest rates on loans and deposits, acts
        as source of pro t for the banks.

        M2: (said thank you and looked convinced and asked other member to proceed)

        M3: You were a part of IIT madras cricket team. So do you know any of the famous cricketers
        who got international fame and who is from IIT Madras.

        *Sir, I’m not able to recall any such name who was part of IIT madras but players like Murali Vijay,
        R Ashwin have a great connection due to SANMAR cricket academy which manages IITM cricket
        ground.

   M3: Okay, there was a famous cricketer, May be you don’t know him. Read about him when you
   go.

   *Sure, sir. And thank you for this unknown insight.

   M3: You also worked for Sashastra Seema Bal, do you know why it was raised?

   *Sir, originally Special Services Bureau (SSB) was raised in December 1963 in the aftermath of
   Indo- China Con ict of 1962 as a civilian force aimed at inculcating the sense of nationalism
   among the border population and to train for defence in times of war.

   M3: And are you aware of the person who was the person behind creating of SSB at that time and
   was also the rst DGP of SSB.

   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Jan 9, 2026 at 9:07 AM]

   M4: you mentioned that you used to stay 8 kms from your coaching in Kota. So how did you
   commute to coaching? Did you use the bicycle?

   *Yes Sir, I used the bicycle to reach the coaching.

   M4: So was it in Kota that you found Cycling as a hobby?

   *No sir, I would say in Kota, using cycle was more of a necessity since rents were very high in the
   closer proximity of the coaching.

   M4: Also, you left SSB and joined RBI. Was it because of your injury or there was any other
   reason?

   *Sir, it was because of my injury.

   M4: You also play cricket. So which format do you like the most?

   *Sir, new formats of cricket are being popularised due to many involving commercialisation but
   personally I like Test Cricket because it is the real test of technique, endurance and mindset.

   M4: Why test match gets over in 3 days these days but earlier it used to take 5 days.

   *Sir, one of the reasons can be the common players who plays both the limited overs crickets and
   test cricket, so the muscle memory kicks in. But these days also we can see test matches ending
   on 5th day like today’s fth Ashes Test between Aus and Eng.

   M4: So what is Bazball cricket??

   *Sir, Bazball cricket refers to the aggressive mindset in England Test Cricket where the batsmen
   try to score fast with a good run rate. This was popularised by the name of England cricket coach
   Brandon Bazz Maccullam.

   M4: So was it the mind set of the players or the coach? Did Bazz played fast for England?

   *Sir, this was because of the name of the coach, and Maccullam played for NewZealand.

   M4: You mentioned that you are working with the RBI, what do you think RBI is to the commercial
   banks? A teacher, A Father or Police?

   *Sir, I’ll say, RBI is more of like a Father to the commercial banks because it not only tells you how
   to grow and do things right, it also gives you the opportunity to rectify their mistakes. It also
   punishes the banks when any grave intentional mistake is committed. Like for a father, the
   success of banks is the success of the RBI. (He seemed quite impressed with the reasoning and
   felt like he went speechless, he said nothing for second before the chairman started asking
   questions again.

   Chairman: So tell me something more about Indian border security forces.

   *Sir, are you with respect to the CAPFs or overall border security?

   Chairman: Tell me about the CAPFs.

   *Sir, starting with the western borders, BSF is there on Indo- Pak borders, then There is ITBP on
   Indo-Tibetan border, SSB on Indo-Nepal and indo- Bhutan borders, then we have Assam Ri es in
   the north east India and Indo- Myanmar border and at last BSF again on the Indo- Bangladesh
   borders.

   Chairman: So there is this FMR concept. Should India ban this totally and what is your stand?

   *Sir, Free Movement Regime (FMR) is the stretch of about 16 kms on Indo- Myanmar border
   where the movement of the local communities was unrestricted. But in the current context of
   increasing security threats like Durg tra cking and safe heaven for the insurgents, it is is prudent
   step by the govt to decide for the total ban, and we have recently completed the fencing in
   Manipur on Myanmar border.
   Sir, I believe that FMR is the necessity in present context but in the long run no border fencing can
   do what human intelligence can. So rather than complete closure, the regulated and strict
   movement can be implemented for indo- Myanmar border with the necessity of VISA/ passport to
   restrict any illegal action across the border.

   Chairman: what is INner line permit system?

   *Sir, ILPS is the system of restricted movement to certain places where isolated communities
   didn’t like to interact with the outsider population. So it was a di erentiated approach for tribal
   populations.

   Chairman: So do you think that has become irrelevant in the present context of increased social
   media penetration in the isolated locations.

https://t.me/csetranscripts/1236
   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Jan 22, 2026 at 9:45 PM]
   Name: ASG
   Board: Raj Shukla Sir
   Keywords: Debating Society President at DU; won best delegate award at a Youth Parliament on
   the Transgender Persons Act, 2019; Meditative mandala doodling; Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, PSIR

   Chairman Sir

   1. So, ASG, you are a political science graduate, are you working currently?
   2. You were a college debating society president. What makes a person a good debater?

   3. I agree about being a good listener and other points, but what else?

   4. Do you know Mr. Sachin Pilot? (I said yes. He then explained Mr. Pilot’s family background,
   especially about his father and how he was not a very uent speaker.) Despite that, what made his
   father win people’s support?

   5. Whose speeches do you enjoy in Parliament? Anyone else? What about PM Modi and Priyanka
   Gandhi? Compare them.

   6. So who is the better speaker PM Modi or Priyanka Gandhi?

   7. What is better in public speaking using the heart or the mind? (He talked a bit about Ram
   Jethmalani and recited a beautiful Urdu shayari, I smiled, I nodded… and I understood almost
   nothing🥲 and then asked me to translate it. I kept staring at him. He said, “You don’t understand
   Urdu?” I replied, “No, sir.” Everyone laughed at my misery. The Chairman himself then translated
   it.)
   7. What does this shayari mean to you?

   M2(female)
   1. I want to put you in a situations. Let’s say you are a Gram Pradhan with 100 households and
   ₹10 crore in funds. How will you function?

   2. But one day, the money will get exhausted. (I said, “That’s where I was about to come, ma’am.”
   She said, “okay, I interrupted please continue.” I then presented a model of a circular village
   economy. She concluded my entire monologue.)

   3. Let’s talk about statistics. How do you think data can be made more acceptable?

   4. But what if the intention is to misguide people how do we tackle that?

   5. So how should data be collected?

   M3

   1. You were part of Bharat Scouts and Guides. How was that experience?

   2. You won Best Delegate at a Youth Parliament on transgender issues. What is your opinion on
   same-sex marriage?

   3. What is the legal and constitutional status of the issue?

   4. Have you heard of GNSS spoo ng? What was the main issue? (I was not con dent here, so I
   humbly declined to go into further discussion.)

   5. Is there any National Waterway in your hometown? What routes does it cover, and what is its
   current status?

   6. Should martial arts be made compulsory for female students in schools?

   M4
   1. Gave a compliment. And asked tell me what made me me say that?
   2. So does being a calm person automatically make someone a better civil servant?
   3. Tell us about your other qualities. (This led to the longest debate I’ve ever had on “risk-taking.”
   He was adamant that bureaucrats are risk-averse people. Others kept laughing.)

   4. Innovation and bureaucracy how do they go together? (Many counter questions)
   5. The UP government has made reading newspapers compulsory in schools. What are your
   views on that? (He said what if kids is reading 3-4 newspapers already on phone, I was like come
   on sir!😶

   M5
   1. You are a public speaker, but I struggle to communicate. How do I break the ice in
   communication?
   2. Your DAF mentions a seminar on “Break the Silence.” (A long discussion followed.)
   3. You mentioned a National Waterway in your hometown. Why is it comparatively less used than
   roads and other means of transport?
   4. What is meditative mandala doodling?
   Chairman Sir again
   1. You had a long discussion on risk-taking. Do you know about the PSLV failure?
   2. He asked some technical jargon. I humbly asked him to exlain. It meant 'to fail in a row in short
   term'. Is it okay to fail repeatedly, or should we wait longer between attempts?
   3. Suppose you are the Defence Secretary what suggestions would you submit in this PSLV
   situation? (He himself answered this.)
   Mocks: Samkalp (good), PW, Sriram IAS, Vision (both faculty-led and bureaucrat-led mocks were
   good), Vajirao

   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Feb 8, 2026 at 8:19 PM]
   Name : Shankaracharya
   Date- 2th Feb 2026. Forenoon. 5th to go(last). Around 25-30 min.

   Chairperson - Honourable Sanjay Verma Sir.

   DAF keywords - Advaita and pratical vedanta, Social issues based movies, Rajasthan, Bikaner,
   Anthropology, B.Sc, changed board from CBSE (10th) to RBSE(12th).

   Said Good afternoon to chairman rst and then all members. Chairman sir asked to have a seat.

   Chairman Sir
   1. Ok shankaracharya, Are you working anywhere?
   2. Do you have any Work-ex? Have you ever been employed?

   3. Just a B.Sc, you never thought of doing any masters, even from an open university. ( Here
   explained Situation during Covid and for job security i prepared for SSC- CGL, then cleared also,
   but didn't join as wanted to give a try for cse).
   4. Chairman sir - Ok Ok, then it's ne. So you are a reader of Advaita and pratical vedanta, don't
   you think it is inapplicable in our present reality. They say that this world is unreal, how you will tell
   this to an aggrieved person as an administrator. Don't you think you have to segregate your
   personal view in professional life? Explained it's not like that, rather very pratical. Unreality or
   mithya is from transcendental pov not from vyhavaric. Then answered the aggrieved qxn, told sir
   that this is exactly what pratical vedanta of swami Vivekanand is. At last he was convinced that it
   covers everything.
   5. Ok, watching socially relevant movies. Don't you think it's making zero impact in the society.
   Films like dhurandhar attracts a large audience whereas only a bunch of people go to watch
   social issues based movies. It's like already progressive people watching progressive movies.
   What's your take on it. Told while commercial element is missing and they attract a fewer
   audience but they do make an impact by increasing awareness ( gave example of menstrual
   hygiene thru padman), removing prejudices and age old biases( Article 15 and Jai bhim), making
   new normal( sitaare zameen par)
   6. Ok, I'll you 100 cr, on which social issue you wud like to make movie on. Told 100 cr is a big
   amount wud like to divide it into various fronts as these movies are low budget and commercial
   element is low. Started saying disability, tribal issues. Chairman interrupted and said these are
   already been made. Give your original perspective or an issue which you have seen. Took a pause
   for 2-3 second and very con dently told 'Men's right' as people are misusing stringent laws and
   making false cases against them. ( Had a look towards lady member here, she was a little
   surprised, i thought I did a blunder here). Chairman sir jokingly said then give me my money back,
   whole room started laughing. He then asked me you wud make movie on an exception ( out of
   100, only 1 case will be of misuse). I told sir increasing awareness about that one is also
   necessary. He looked satis ed but I don't know. This answer can land anyside.

   Member- 1.

   7. So you are from Bikaner, do you think Rajasthan in general and bikaner in particular have
   'Colonial mindset'. I started answering and got little diverted, then chairman sir interrupted and
   said you didn't hear the qxn properly.
   8. Then we talk about royalty mindset in bikaner rather than colonial mindset. Chairman sir said
   it's very feudal mindset. I said de nitely It is but nowadays it is changing, MLA, MP are rising from

   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Feb 8, 2026 at 8:47 PM]
   Name : Shankaracharya
   Date- 2th Feb 2026. Forenoon. 5th to go(last). Around 25-30 min.

   Chairperson - Honourable Sanjay Verma Sir.

   DAF keywords - Advaita and pratical vedanta, Social issues based movies, Rajasthan, Bikaner,
   Anthropology, B.Sc, changed board from CBSE (10th) to RBSE(12th).

   Said Good afternoon to chairman rst and then all members. Chairman sir asked to have a seat.

   Chairman Sir
   1. Ok shankaracharya, Are you working anywhere?
   2. Do you have any Work-ex? Have you ever been employed?
   3. Just a B.Sc, you never thought of doing any masters, even from an open university. ( Here
   explained Situation during Covid and for job security i prepared for SSC- CGL, then cleared also,
   but didn't join as wanted to give a try for cse).

   4. Chairman sir - Ok Ok, then it's ne. So you are a reader of Advaita and pratical vedanta, don't
   you think it is inapplicable in our present reality. They say that this world is unreal, how you will tell
   this to an aggrieved person as an administrator. Don't you think you have to segregate your
   personal view in professional life? Explained it's not like that, rather very pratical. Unreality or
   mithya is from transcendental pov not from vyhavaric. Then answered the aggrieved qxn, told sir
   that this is exactly what pratical vedanta of swami Vivekanand is. At last he was convinced that it
   covers everything.
   5. Ok, watching socially relevant movies. Don't you think it's making zero impact in the society.
   Films like dhurandhar attracts a large audience whereas only a bunch of people go to watch
   social issues based movies. It's like already progressive people watching progressive movies.
   What's your take on it. Told while commercial element is missing and they attract a fewer
   audience but they do make an impact by increasing awareness ( gave example of menstrual
   hygiene thru padman), removing prejudices and age old biases( Article 15 and Jai bhim), making
   new normal( sitaare zameen par)
   6. Ok, I'll you 100 cr, on which social issue you wud like to make movie on. Told 100 cr is a big
   amount wud like to divide it into various fronts as these movies are low budget and commercial
   element is low. Started saying disability, tribal issues. Chairman interrupted and said these are
   already been made. Give your original perspective or an issue which you have seen. Took a pause
   for 2-3 second and very con dently told 'Men's right' as people are misusing stringent laws and
   making false cases against them. ( Had a look towards lady member here, she was a little
   surprised, i thought I did a blunder here). Chairman sir jokingly said then give me my money back,
   whole room started laughing. He then asked me you wud make movie on an exception ( out of
   100, only 1 case will be of misuse). I told sir increasing awareness about that one is also
   necessary. He looked satis ed but I don't know. This answer can land anyside.

   Member- 1.

   7. So you are from Bikaner, do you think Rajasthan in general and bikaner in particular have
   'Colonial mindset'. I started answering and got little diverted, then chairman sir interrupted and
   said you didn't hear the qxn properly.
   8. Then we talk about royalty mindset in bikaner rather than colonial mindset. Chairman sir said
   it's very feudal mindset. I said de nitely It is but nowadays it is changing, MLA, MP are rising from
   ground and at the same time royal leaders did good development( mention of Gang canal by
   Maharaja Ganga singh which inspired formation of Indira Gandhi canal).
   9. Can you explain why did you change your board from CBSE to RBSE as CBSE is considered
   superior?

   Member- 2( Woman)

   10. What are recent changes in climate of Rajasthan due to Climate change and global warming.
   ( Mentioned deserti cation and rising frequency of extreme climate events like heat waves, erratic
   rainfall etc)

   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Feb 9, 2026 at 10:25 PM]
   Name: Saul Goodman
   Date: 03/02/2026 (Forenoon, First to go)
   Duration: Around 30 minutes
   Key DAF Details: NAME, BELAGAVI,JAWAHAR NAVODAYA VIDYALAYA, KARNATKA, CRICKET,
   MECHANICAL ENGINEERING, ANTHROPOLOGY (nothing was asked from other keywords)

   Board: Shri B B SWAIN sir

   Questions asked:
    Entered room and greeted everyone.

   Chairperson:
   1) How are you? Is it very cold outside? ( It was very much cold outside that morning)
   2) (while looking at my DAF) So you're from NAVODAYA school?
   3) How are these schools? Have they bene tted rural areas?
   4) What are the things you like in NAVODAYA schools?
   (While I was answering, he too added points about Migration policy of these schools)
   5) Have you been part of migration policy of Navodaya schools?
   6) Do they give coaching for exams like NEET or competitive exams?

   M1:
   1) You're Mechanical Engineer by background, why you chose Anthropology?
   2) you chose it because it's scoring(Though I didn't mention anything about scores in previous
   question)? How much is average score?
   3) How will anthropology help you in civil services?
   4) Tell me few drawbacks or areas of improvement Navodaya schools?
   5) what are the extra curricular activities they teach you in NAVODAYA?

   M2:
   1) What is the meaning of your name? ( When I began answering, he too added about NANDI,
   GOD SHIVA relating to my name)
   2) You watch cricket then tell me, between watching cricket and playing cricket, which one is
   better?
   3) How many teams are playing in this T20 worldcup?
   4) How has this preparation journey shaped your personality?
   5)What keeps you engaged apart from this preparation?

   M3: ( It was lengthy conversation)
   1) Read my name and asked what your friends call you?
   2) what reforms do you suggest for UPSC? (Interrupted my answer when I said about attempts)
   3) Don't you think Indian Youths are wasting their prime time in these exams? Over 10lakh sit for
   this exam.. what about them? They could have contributed elsewhere.
   He also mentioned about Pratibha Setu.
   4) What should we do to engage youth apart from preparation?
   4) should we limit number of attempts and reduce age?
   5)How about conducting one single exam for all the the posts and selecting people from that
   pool?
   6) You're from Belagavi, tell me what's the status of Belagavi Dispute with Maharashtra?
   I told about Mahajan commission..he then asked about what are the names of villages that
   commission told to swap with Maharashtra.
   7) Tell me why your Talluk is famous for?
   8) Since you are Mechanical Engineer, tell me the di erence between Clearance and Tolerance?
   9) How these both are important in public service?
   It was very long conversation, sir was still asking then chairman sir interrupted and told other
   member to continue.

   M4: ( Female member)
   1)( asked question about my answer to member1) are Navodaya in rural areas a blessing or
   negative thing?
   2) How do they help rural areass?
   3) Have you read today's newspaper? What was most important headline? ( US india deal was
   announced last night)
   4) I told about the deal...she asked is it a deal or declaration?
   5) Tell me about Board of Peace.
   6) Is UN Dead? Should we scrap it?
   7)UN Reforms

   After this, Chairman sir told your interview is over and anything you would ask? ..
   Then he said, All The Best.

   Board was cordial. It was very much di erent from what I experienced in mocks.
   Overall a good experience.
   Daily discussion with peers helped a lot.
   Mocks/O20 (If any): La Excellence (special thanks to them for helping in early stages of interview
   prep), Sankalp,Vajiram, Vajirao,NEXT IAS, SRIRAM IAS, QUANTEL.

   (SRIRAM IAS) , Mahesh Bhagwat Sir (Detailed DAF Discussion), Shubham Sir -Vidyapeeth IAS
   ( for Structuring answers) .

https://t.me/csetranscripts/1354
   Interview Transcripts (CSPT-2025), [Feb 10, 2026 at 4:50 PM]
   Name: Murphy's Law
   Date : 3/02/2026, Afternoon. 3rd To go.
   Duration: not sure, was waiting for around 5-10 min outside (was called 10 -12 minutes before
   3PM), Exit time i saw the clock: 3:35PM
   Board: Had no idea- some ma'am i didn't recognise- as I haven't seen any of their pro le,plus
   couldn't spot any name on cabin before entering- later asked the person who escorted me.

   DAF: Civil Engineering, PSIR, Gaya, Bihar, Jharkhand. Nothing else asked.
   Greeted everyone, Ma'am asked me to take my seat.

   Ma'am read my DAF and pointed out towards my work experience with an aggregator.

   Ma'am: Are you still working?
   I said no ma'am. (worked till July 2025).

   Ma'am: But you worked for quite sometime here.
   I said yes ma'am.
   Ma'am: Is this work related to civil engineering?
   I Said no ma'am. It dealt with Time Value of Money.
   She said okay. (i expected a related question as 5 years i did that job)

   Ma'am: So, Murphy's Law- Help me understand this. You are a civil engineer, India is a hot
   climate country yet we have this trend of glass buildings. Why?

   (First question itself bouncer for me, given 5+ years gap with Engineering). I couldn't think beyond
   asthetics.And it wasn't very engineering answer so i didn't said that.
   Gave 2 points (1 was horribly wrong)
   1. ma'am we also have a lot of dust and it could help in such structures. (realised as soon as
   those words left my mouth that it was a senseless point).
   ma'am: Dust can be blocked by concrete walls as well. Plus glass gets dirty.
   I said Yes ma'am.
   2. In some buildings modi ed glass looking facade is used to act as solar panels as well.

   She nodded , but wasn't fully convinced (as i am sure this wasn't the right explanation)

   I then added sorry' ma'am i cannot think of any other engineering justi cation as of now. (as soon
   as i saw the rst glass building after returning from UPSC bhavan - it struck me; Material costs are
   key consideration here since steel is more expensive and is integral to modern concrete
   constructions so glass does o er little glass advantage by limiting use of steel and concrete to
   just frame)

   Ma'am: Okay tell me what are Green buildings.

   I said, buildings that are sustainable. Both- during their construction - using low carbon process
   and materials, as well as during their operations and life cycle.

   Ma'am: Tell me some elements of Green buildings. Assuming construction phase has used
   sustainable process.

   I said: 1. Clean air conditioning and heating. 2. Using Footsteps and activities in the building to
   generate some power. 3. Treating and re-using Grey Water.
   Ma'am interjected and asked- Treated water, meaning rain water harvesting?
   I said ma'am Rain water harvesting is a part, but by Grey water -i mean - water from toilets being
   treated and re used for non drinking purposes like gardening and cleaning.

   She seemed convinced.

   Ma'am: So you live in Jharkhand. Must have heard about Jamtara. How do we prevent such
   things if you are posted in any district of Jharkhand?

   I said - Ma'am the people involved in Jamtara were mostly footsoldiers. And operated at behest of
   outside criminal networks like the ones in south east asia. So awareness will be a key tool in
   combating.

   1. We can make people aware of the same so that they don't fell prey to such criminal networks.
   2.Also to make them aware of negative consequences on their life. Being on wrong side of the law
   can ruin lives as well.
   3. Timely detection.I explained using a recent Bihar example where authorities detected a person
   using Sim Box of 20,000 Sim and defrauded thousands - by tracking abnormal power utilisation.

   Ma'am asked how will you spread awareness!?
   I said since mostly from rural areas these people are, can take help from local Panchayats- as
   there is more ground level connect of local leaders to people.
   Also Civil Society organisations.

   (Social media should have been an important part here but didn't even occur to me till i left the
   room- many such moments will be there throughout the PT)

   availability of water throughout.

   However it has some issues.
   1. We don't have truly water surplus rivers beyond himalyan rivers. Most are monsoon dependent
   and these days monsoon is very erratic to give any predictability for water availability. (Can have

   Bihar has good potential at MSME level - (i wanted to link SHGs but forgot in midst)- used the
   example of food processing potential. Talked about Makhana. How Bihar is home to most

   Next, as sir mentioned bihar has skilled and talented people, we can explore domains like o ering

   Another point i would like to add, is exploring Bihar's huge potential in tourism sector. We have
   buddhist circuit, Mahabodhi temple etc that can also boost the state.

   just pause and think on templates - somehow felt unnatural)

   Said- Sorry sir. मुझे इसका                                                 नन ।

   सर ने कहा कोई बात न । Ma'am then indicated next member

   M4:
   So you are a civil engineer (🥲 )

   We observe this issues of poor construction quality. Why is it that we have poor quality compared
   to British era structures.

   I Said - sir one prime reason that i can think of is we follow Project based approach in india. where
   demand for engineers peak during construction phase.

   On the other hand the idea should be to have life cycle based approach. Where engineers are
   engaged throughout the life cycle of any structure not just construction. It is followed in
   developed countries.
   I added NHAI has started doing it.

   Then he started talking about the bridges - Indore, Mumbai and added in Bihar it's common for
   bridges to fail.

   I said - Sir in the context the Bhopal 90degree Bridge (sir said yes Bhopal). Bridges do not get
   constructed in matter of days. it takes 2-3 years. And there is usually regular audit. It seems it was
   not properly done otherwise the issue would have been agged.

   So who do you hold accountable? The contractor would say i am executing the design given.

   I said, sir we need to identify at what levels lapses have been there. Right from design to
   execution and audit. And need to x accountability at every level.

   Then again - Why does it happen?

   I said we also have very high tolerance for non compliance in some areas.
   (Ma'am raised eyebrows with a grin -and the sir who asked - other members also changed their
   facial expressions from smiling poker face to wider grin and maybe mild surprise/shock on me
   uttering those words)

   Sir asked-

   North Bihar is ood prone. Are you aware we are constructing a medical College there.
   I said yes sir- AIIMS Darbhanga.

   How do you construct in a ood prone area.

   I said- if we have to construct in a water logged situation; can explore co er dam to halt water
   and do the foundation work like we do in case of river bridges.

   Sir said - Co er Dam will last only one year or so then what?

   I said we need to have elevated structures on piers or basement having provision for ood waters
   to pass as is followed in Japan. However for that there needs to be complete interconnectedness
   of drainage system in the municipality. ( Maybe he wanted to know about identi cation of areas

               Sir- What is the process to be followed in construction? Do we just do tendering and start??

               I said - Sir we start with feasibility study. For example - if we want to construct a road, need to
                 rst asess requirement, tra c studies and see if feasible to construct at that area.

               Next do preliminary survey.
               (sir said - something related to one step i can't recall but i had said, yes sir it will be part of
               feasibility studies)
               After that design phase and follow up with tendering, then execution.

               Ma'am said - Thank You your interview is over you can go. I thanked everyone and left.

               I felt that conversation was not long maybe 20minutes. But then
               Glanced at clock while getting up from chair - It was 3:35PM. Had not checked the clock while
               entering (was zoned out)

               Maybe i entered around 3PM as i was escorted 10 -12 minutes before 3PM from waiting area and
               waited for 5-10 minutes outside. (Don't know time feels di erent there) so I guess around 30
               minutes

               Asked the person escorting me back - Kinka board tha. He said with surprise - Suman Sharma
               Ma'am ka. ( am I cooked 🥲 ?)

               Ignorance is bliss 😄 🤣 . But it made sense. Felt board had an idea what all i could be well
               prepared as we are in the third phase so no point asking "easy questions" 🥲 ( budget, Hobbies,
               Work, IR) so they leaned towards one weak link- civil engineering (as i had no connection with it
               for 5+ years and no related work experience) So might have theoretical knowledge of the subject
               (which i did and had prepared in last 50 days or so-but not other practical aspects)

               Fumbled a bit in 2-3 places.
               While answering glanced at others occassionally - everyone was listening. Ma'am was noting
               down stu here and there. Some members too.

               Felt very di erent from mocks. Even questions were not in QnA format but just conversation - so
               couldn't just go with template made answers. But in hindsight some aspects like; Jamtara , Bihar
               qs and quality of construction - could have been better tackled (This will always be the regret no
               matter what)

               Very cordial and comfortable board.

               Mocks; Vajiram, Vajirao and Reddy,Vision Ias, Samkalp (2), Sriram IAS, Ekagra IAS, NACS Bihar
               Jharkhand, CMP O2O

               Peer Discussion with my mains group friends.
               Non UPSC Friends - helped in analysis other aspects through Mock videos feedback.

   Name: Gudakesh

   Date: February 13, 2026 (AN, 3rd to go)

   Key DAF Details: Darbhanga, Bihar, Kota, Anthropology, IIT Roorkee, Hatha Yoga, Hindi Poetry
   (Rest not relevant)

   Board: Sanjay Verma

   Questions asked:
   The table was being cleaned when I was asked to enter. All the members are standing around the
   table. I ask for permission, enter, and greet the panel.

   M1 remarks that we are standing for your welcome. I smile.
   Chairperson asks do you have any issues if we continue the interview standing?
   M1 remarks that the candidate practises hatha yoga.
   Chairman says if you perform a headstand for the whole duration of the interview, I'd award you
   20 marks extra.
   M3 asks which kind of yoga do you do in hatha yoga. He further asks which asanas do you do?
   M3 and M1 engage in a discussion over what does the term 'hatha' mean. I was listening to them.

   The chairperson then signalled us all to sit.

   Chairperson:
   1. Tell us what 'Hatha' mean in hatha yoga. (Question continued from previous conversation
   between M1 and M3)
   2. Yoga started as a quest for moksha, but now it has been reduced to physical activity only.
   Why?
   3. Where would you go for your honeymoon?
   4. You have stayed at multiple places, it suggests that you are a risk taker.
   5. Out of all the places you have stayed, at which place did the water taste the best?
   6. Aside all the serious stu you have written in your DAF, what is it you are truly passionate
   about?
   7. Tell me the di erence in the poetry of Gulzar Sahab and Swanand Kirkire? (remarked later that
   Gulzar sahab has a monopoly on the Moon since long before NASA even thought of venturing out
   in space)

   M1:
   1. What is Darbhanga famous for?
   2. Monologue on stray dog issue in Delhi, how would you tackle as Muicipal commisisoner? (2
   follow ups regarding SC decision, and capacity constraints)
   3. Discussion on ghettoization of students due to coaching industry in places like Kota. I
   responded with adaptive testing suggested by IIT Council, and how normalisation of scores could
   help reduce the pressure. M1 remarked that the same could be suggested for UPSC Interview. All
   laughed. M2 suggested that interview is easier. Chairperson remarked that Prelims is the toughest
   these days. I was smiling.

   M2:
   1. Situational question - you decided something but upon discussion with your subordinates, who
   presented an alternative view, you changed your decision. This happens thrice in a row. What
   would you do? What would you think of yourself? Would it not be a question on your
   competency? What about seeking a transfer?
   2. What is Happiness Index?
   3. Which country is at the top? (I remembered Bhutan as tha happiest, so said I think Bhutan)
   4. What about Scandinavian countries?
   5. Where is India ranked approximately?
   6. What is one panacea which can ensure happiness for everyone? (Suggested that ful lment in
   work based on capabilities and opportunities can be one thing which could ensure happiness of
   all)

   M3:
   1. Which place are we sitting right now? Are you here for the rst time?

        2. Which building is right next to it? Said sir not sure about the directions - said one which is on
        left while coming to Dholpur house. I responded that I am not aware Sir. He answered that you
        have studied at the place on which it is named. I said sir Kota house. He remarked that no extra
        marks for this answer as I had hinted xD
        3. Is there a Darbhanga House in Delhi?
        4. Why are there Darbhanga houses in many places across the country? (M1 jokingly remarked
        that they must be rich)
        5. If o ered Moksha right now, would you accept?
        6. Where is Bihar school of yoga located?
        7. What is their unique contribution?
        8. What is Yoga nidra?
        9. Why do people do it?
        10. Have you heard of Kundalini?
        11. What is the physical manifestation of Kundalini awakening?

   Key DAF Details: Economics graduation and optional, following international a airs as hobby,

   Board: Dinesh Dasa sir

   Questions asked:

   Chairperson:
   1. Asked me to introduce myself and why I was learning Chinese

   then asked if the government could do something to leverage the sky high market prices of gold
   and monetise the same. I recounted the South Korean example of a similar activity in 1997 during
   the IMF crisis (although that involved donation), talked about o ering gold loans for idle assets so
   as to boost consumption in the economy, but also the fact that there is an emotional angle
   attached to Indian women keeping gold as savings so they may not part with it easily. Somehow
   despite a long conversation on this sir kept countering but he was smiling throughout the
   interview

                  Member 2:
                  1. Said it wasn't related to the interview but asked why I was wearing a blazer over a saree. I had
                  seen this question before in a transcript but at the time I could only say that it was cold today
                  (since it had rained early in the morning). Sir laughed and said me too
                  2. Discussion on Quad and its wavering momentum, whether we should continue in the present
                  form or head towards securitisation. Counter questions on the same. When I tried to take a middle
                  path (because I genuinely felt so) and explained my rationale, he said China is already hostile
                  towards all so why not go for full securitisation. I said something along the lines of preventing
                  undue con ict would be in the best interest of all
                  3. Asked about some naval event happening in South India. Somehow I completely skipped the
                  full page ad in the newspaper talking about it which didn't go down very well. Conversation went
                  on regarding maritime security
                  4. Long discussion regarding the Board of Peace and whether I think it will be successful or not

                  Member 3:
                  1. Asked if I know the amount of gold that male and female individuals can hold (I couldn't
                  remember the exact value) then told me himself. A follow up question on this that I can't
                  remember
                  2. Monologue on how 99.5% of candidates fail and yet people keep wasting their youth on UPSC
                  (perhaps because it was my 4th attempt). Asked what can be done about this so I answered both
                  from the perspective of one of these aspirants as well as an economist's but his expression was
                  changing the entire time so I don't know if he was satis ed with the answer

                  [After this Dasa sir said that I can leave. I found it quite strange because two panel members
                  hadn't asked anything. As I stood up to leave, the other panel members pointed out that fact as
                  well so they asked me to sit down again]

                  Member 4:
                  1. Wanted to know why USD is the world's reserve currency and which grouping has been talking
                  about challenging that. (At this point Dasa sir said we've already asked too much of economics so
                  you can choose another topic if you want. Since I knew the theme I went with it.)
                  2. Again wanted to know why I was learning Chinese but kept interrupting

                  [Member 5 didn't ask anything. Dasa sir said that he was a professor of economics so he only

              6. All the CJIs keep saying that Bail is Norm and what not why doesn't it translate on the ground?
